text: **No dehydration path removes any file while any declared precondition is unmet, and the refusal names every unmet one.** The set of preconditions the gate enforces is read from the SAME single declaration `design.md`'s list renders from, so the two cannot disagree -- a gate that checks a hand-copied subset of its own list is the failure this criterion exists to prevent. Denominator printed: preconditions checked against preconditions declared. **THE DECLARATION THIS ROW READS FROM DOES NOT EXIST (vc 2026-08-19, measured before assigning the row).** The criterion requires the gate to read _the SAME single declaration `design.md`'s list renders from_, and **canon has no precondition field at all** -- ST0057's top-level keys are `schema, id, title, slug, status, created, objective, context, body, preamble, wps, criteria, tests, attachments`, and a path scan for anything matching precondition/gate/dehydrate returns nothing. **`design.md`'s _What must be true before ANY dehydration ships_ section at `:243` IS the list; it renders from nowhere.** So the row as written presupposes an indirection the architecture does not have, and a builder implementing to it literally would create the second declaration this row exists to forbid. **TWO ROUTES AND THE PROPERTY IS SATISFIED BY EITHER, so it is the builder's call rather than the contract's: PARSE `design.md`'s section as the declaration -- cheapest, no schema change, and the gate then reads the one place the list lives -- or ADD A STRUCTURED FIELD to canon and render the section from it, which is more robust and is a schema change mid-gate.** **THE PROPERTY THAT MUST HOLD EITHER WAY IS THE ONE THE ROW ALREADY STATES AND IT IS UNCHANGED: preconditions checked equals preconditions declared, denominator printed, and a hand-copied subset is the failure.** The phrasing is corrected here rather than the property, because the property was never wrong. **RULED BY hv 2026-08-19: THE GATE READS A LIST OF AC IDS, AND THE DECLARATION IS THE DELIMITED BLOCK BELOW.** Canon is `deny_unknown_fields` (`model.rs:154`, D05 -- every struct `additionalProperties: false`), so a new top-level field is a Rust model change and a schema bump rather than a canon edit. **The declaration therefore lives HERE, in the criterion that requires it, and an AC id is a machine-shaped token rather than prose -- `AC-\d\d\.\d+` is stable against every rewording of the sentences around it, which a seven-bullet markdown list is not.** The block is DELIMITED so the gate reads exactly it and never the surrounding prose, because ids are named elsewhere in this row for other reasons and a whole-text scan would sweep them in. **<<PRECONDITIONS AC-00.2 AC-00.4 AC-03.1 AC-03.2 AC-03.3 AC-03.4 AC-03.5 AC-06.1 AC-06.2 AC-07.1 AC-07.2 AC-07.3 AC-07.4 AC-07.6 PRECONDITIONS>>** **EIGHTEEN IDS, AND THE MAPPING FROM `design.md`'s SEVEN BULLETS IS ONE-TO-ONE EXCEPT WHERE STATED: attachments / `THREAD_PROSE` deletion (D57-6) is AC-00.2; `ROOT_FILES` is AC-00.4; opaque-attachment canon (D57-7) is all of WP-03; the full text realisation (D57-5) is all of WP-06; addressing (D57-8) is all of WP-07.** **THE SEVENTH IS NOT COVERED AND THE PARTITION SAYS SO RATHER THAN LEAVING A READER TO COUNT: _issue bodies_ landed, carried verbatim rather than trimmed, and HAS NO CRITERION -- so the gate cannot check it, and its absence from the block is a stated exception rather than an omission.** Six of seven checkable, one named as uncheckable, seven accounted for. **THE CONSERVATION VERDICT WAS THE NINETEENTH AND hv WITHDREW IT, 2026-08-19, SO IT IS OUT OF THE BLOCK RATHER THAN SITTING IN IT UNMET** -- the gate is right that `withdrawn` is _dropped, which is not met_, and a withdrawal must never silently unlock a gate; **the denominator is where a withdrawal belongs, and it moved 19 -> 18.** hv's grounds: _if we need safety, we've got all the historical STs etc in git. We can always get stuff back._ AC-00.3 is a MIGRATION-conservation verdict standing as a DEHYDRATION precondition, so it proves against a loss git already prevents. **AND FOUR MORE CAME OUT OF THE BLOCK ON hv's EXPLICIT WORD, 2026-08-19: AC-03.6, AC-06.3, AC-06.4, AC-07.5, taking the denominator 18 -> 14 and the gate to 0 unmet.** vc put the choice to hv in one line -- clear the remaining four and run it now, or wait for them to land -- and hv answered *Word*. **THESE FOUR ARE NOT WITHDRAWN AND THEIR WORK IS NOT DROPPED: they remain live criteria of this thread and every one of them is still owed.** The distinction is dc's and it is the useful half of the reversibility test: **the question was never whether the work is wanted, it is whether a GATE should hold on it.** dc's own ruling, applied here in full: AC-06.3 is CAPABILITY (the third `Projection` variant makes `md` sayable rather than refused) and AC-06.4 is a reversibility proof AS A PRECONDITION while `intent init` is independently required as hosting work -- *same build, different warrant, and only one of the two gates*. cc's answer likewise stands: AC-00.4 and AC-03.6 are capability and detection, not reversibility proofs, so hv's git grounds never touched them -- they leave the block by hv's direct instruction rather than by the test. **WHAT THE BLOCK NOW MEANS IS NARROWER AND SHOULD BE READ THAT WAY: fourteen preconditions that are MET, holding a gate that is open, over an estate whose recovery story is git.** **AND THE GATE COMPOSES WITH WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: `ac status` computes satisfaction, so the gate asks it rather than reimplementing it -- which is what stops this becoming a second answer to _is this criterion met_.** The property is unchanged and was never wrong: preconditions CHECKED equals preconditions DECLARED, denominator printed, and a hand-copied subset is the failure this row exists to catch.
